title: Silver in Women's 10m Air Rifle Opens India's Asian Games Account
excerpt: Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod finished second behind a world-record China on Day 1 at Aichi-Nagoya, while Suchika Tariyal assured India of its first-ever Asian Games MMA medal.
body:
• India's first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games came on Day 1: silver in the women's 10m air rifle team event, with Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod totalling 1898.0 points.
  • China took gold with a world record 1904.2; Japan finished third at 1897.1. Valarivan also qualified for the individual final and later won a second silver there.
  • Suchika Tariyal assured India's first-ever Asian Games MMA medal by reaching the women's 60kg semifinal, while the women's hockey team thrashed Uzbekistan 19–0.

India is on the board at the 20th Asian Games. On the opening day of competition at Aichi-Nagoya, the women's 10m air rifle team of Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod won silver, finishing behind a world-record Chinese team — the first Indian medal of the Games and a reminder of where the country's shooting programme stands in the continental pecking order.

The trio totalled 1898.0 points. China won gold with 1904.2 — a new world record in the team event — while Japan took bronze at 1897.1, less than a point behind India. Valarivan shot 633.5 in qualification and advanced to the individual final alongside Maskar, where she went on to win a second silver for India.

"This was absolutely expected. It was one of our strong events — China, Korea, India all neck to neck."

— Ronak Pandit, High Performance Manager, Indian shooting team, speaking to ANI

President Droupadi Murmu led the congratulations on X: "Heartiest congratulations to Elavenil Valarivan, Vidarsa K Vinod and Sonam Uttam Maskar on winning Silver Medal... Your commendable achievement has opened India's medal account at the Games and brings immense pride to the nation." Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya also hailed the trio.

A strong event, as expected

Shooting has long been India's most reliable Asian Games discipline, and the women's 10m air rifle team event was flagged as a top medal prospect before the Games opened. Ronak Pandit, the team's High Performance Manager, told ANI the silver was "absolutely expected," describing the event as "very tight" with China, Korea and India "neck to neck." He added that "one of our stronger shooters was in the second relay and she did pretty well" — a result the team was happy with, though the world record from China underlined how steep the standard at the top has become.

A first for Indian MMA

Day 1 also delivered a milestone in a sport making its Asian Games debut. Suchika Tariyal beat Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2–0 in the women's traditional 60kg quarterfinal to reach the semifinals — assuring India of its first-ever Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts, since both semifinalists medal. The colour of that medal will be decided in the coming days.

MMA's inclusion at Aichi-Nagoya is part of the Games' gradual expansion into combat sports with global followings, and every MMA medal at these Games is automatically a national first for the country that wins it.

Around the venues

Elsewhere on Day 1, India's women's hockey team opened with a 19–0 demolition of Uzbekistan — the kind of scoreline that signals intent in a sport where India is chasing gold. Both the men's and women's table tennis teams beat Indonesia 3–0 to open their team campaigns.

There was disappointment in teqball, where Quimcy Dsouza lost his semifinal on September 19, ending India's bid for gold in the sport's newest discipline. Teqball, like MMA, reflects the Games' expanding roster — and India's uneven footing across it.

What's next

The silver sets an early tone: India is competitive in its core disciplines but chasing a China that keeps rewriting the record books. The shooting programme has more events to come, the hockey campaigns are underway, and Tariyal's MMA semifinal will decide whether Day 1's guaranteed medal turns gold. With kabaddi starting September 21 and athletics to follow, the medal table is just getting started.
